shape: a 24-bit signed accumulator machine over a byte-indexed table at $9800

routines.$99D2: compare table[Y] against table[X]: A register +1 / 0 / -1, signed
routines.$9A65: ACC := table[Y] * 256 / table[X], |remainder| in EXT; no guard on either edge, and the domain is the quotient fitting 24 bits
routines.$9C5C: ACC := table[Y]; Y += 3; X preserved via $EE

gate: the movement block is gated on $0948, set by paddle 1 below $5A while WARP ($81F3) is not exhausted; at rest MATH is never called

results.what: the oracle reaches flight, with MATH resident
$9C5C loads ACC from table[Y], advances Y by 3 and parks X in $EE
$9C6C loads B from table[X], and leaves X at zero with Y at X+3
$9C7A stores ACC into table[Y] and advances Y by 3
and it does not zero the entry - that reading only held because ACC was zero
$9C4B copies table[X] to table[Y] without touching ACC, advancing both by 3
$999B adds table[X] to ACC, wrapping at 24 bits
it accumulates across calls, which is why reading it as a function of the table failed
and the A register it leaves is not the entry high byte once ACC is non-zero
$99AB loads both and leaves ACC = table[Y] - table[X]
$9A08 negates ACC in place
$99D2 compares table[Y] against table[X] as signed 24-bit
and it is signed - these pairs would come out the other way unsigned
$9A65 divides table[Y]*256 by table[X] into ACC
results.detail: 225 pairs over the whole sign square, 0 outside 24 bits

results.what: and leaves the remainder in EXT as a magnitude, never negated
concretely: -1000/3 and 1000/3 leave the same remainder with opposite quotients
the sign flag $CE records whether the operands disagreed
the control cases are ones where these three variants actually differ
control: it does not floor
control: nor use a signed remainder
control: nor clamp to the signed range
a zero divisor is not checked: every trial subtraction succeeds, so ACC fills with ones
the domain is the QUOTIENT fitting 24 bits, not the numerator
past 24 bits the quotient SATURATES to $FFFFFF - it does not wrap into the register
results.detail: 11 overflowing divides, all $FFFFFF with the sign fix-up applied, and a wrapping model disagrees with every one

results.what: with paddle 1 at rest the gate stays closed, so the MOVEMENT block never divides
but MATH runs whatever the gate does - the rest of the loop drives it every pass
results.detail: 8 entry points reached and 19 divides with the gate shut, which is the range and bearing blocks and $1C3D

results.what: paddle 1 below $5A opens the gate and the movement block starts dividing too
every division the movement block performs stays inside the domain
results.detail: 4 divides from the movement block, none past 24 bits - a few passes is evidence, not a proof, so the port still models both edges

results.what: $9998 loads ACC and then adds, so it is the whole add where $999B is only its tail
and that is what separates them: the same call gives 1007 against 507
$9A17 leaves ACC = table[Y] * table[X] / 256, with the discarded byte in $F9
$9A04 tests the sign bit and falls into the negate, so it is an absolute value
but not quite - the negate wraps, so the most negative value comes back negative
it agrees with trunc(sqrt(ACC * 256)) across the range
except at ACC = 1, where the first halving reaches zero and the equality test fires
results.detail: 1 gives 0, where the closed form gives 16 - which is why the port runs the loop

results.what: and it takes no magnitude, so ACC = -1 is rooted as the pattern $FFFFFF
every answer is a whole number of degrees
and the range is 0 to 90
it is monotonic, which is what lets the port describe it by its step boundaries
and it is NOT trunc(atan) - the series has its own rounding, high and low
results.detail: 52 of 496 inputs disagree with a trunc(atan) model

results.what: some whole degrees are skipped entirely, which no closed form would predict
results.detail: 4 from the step boundaries, 4 confirmed in the machine

results.what: a negative ratio gives a negative angle of the same size
nothing reads B, EXT, R3 or R7 after an arctangent - the next MATH call reloads them
results.detail: so the port modelling only ACC there is a limitation nothing can observe

results.what: the listing is present and holds enough call sites to conclude anything
every call site sets the indices it uses, so the index exits are not a contract
results.detail: 0 of 229 inherit an index - the port models no index bookkeeping
